newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Legalise narcotics, says ruler of tiny Liechtenstein.
newsitem.headline: Legalise narcotics, says ruler of tiny Liechtenstein.

text.p: The ruling prince of tiny Liechtenstein, one of Europe's last governing monarchs, on Monday said the world war on drugs had failed and urged states to legalise narcotics under supervision.

Prince Hans Adam II said in a Swiss newspaper interview he believed hard drugs such as heroin and cocaine should be distributed by the state to adults in special narcotics rooms under state supervision.
"The drug policy that we have followed for years at a high cost has failed," the prince told the daily St Galler Tagblatt about world-wide efforts to supress drugs use.
"This has led to nothing other than drug cartels and the mafia amassing huge profits. We did not pay attention to the law of the market," he added.

Hans Adam said governments should cut organised crime out of the business by buying narcotics straight from the producers at prices higher than crime gangs pay and selling them at street prices at home.
Asked whether he thought more people would use drugs if they were easier to get, the prince answered:
"It is already very easy to get them, because the mafia has set up an enormous distribution network due to the high profits and has also targeted schools," he said.
Hans Adam, aged 52, said hashish cigarettes were already being sold in school when he was a pupil.
"But I never had enough pocket money," he said.

The prince, who has executive power in his principality between Switzerland and Austria, said Liechtenstein was too small to start any such legalisation alone in the face of United Nations and other world accords against narcotics.
Leichtenstein's drugs laws are comparable to most in Western Europe, prohibiting narcotics trade and use under penalty of jail terms or fines.

Liechtenstein, covering an area of 62 square miles (160 sq km), is a political hybrid -- a constitutional hereditary monarchy. It has a 25-strong parliament whose legislation requires assent from the head of state.
